lines.trans: Tell me, how are you feeling right now?
Thank you, I feel quite alright.
Doctor, does that mean everything is fine with him?
Yes, everything will be fine, he needs to lie down for a bit.
He needs to lie down so the dizziness passes.

lines.trans: He has no fractures, which is actually amazing!
Do not jump from the third floor like that anymore!
Thank you very much for your help, doctor.
Vika, forgive me that things turned out this way.
It is nothing, I missed my meeting because of you.
Alright, friends, let's start rehearsing our plan!
In walks Dima's friend, Lyova, go!

examples.trans: Max, stop it, I do not want to hear anything more!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be late', paired with 'опаздывать'.

examples.text: Да ничего, я опоздала на встречу из-за тебя.
examples.trans: It is nothing, I missed my meeting because of you.

examples.text: Прости, я опоздал.
examples.trans: Sorry, I'm late.

examples.text: Мы не опоздаем?
examples.trans: Won't we be late?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как говорил один мудрец, солнце светит всем одинаково.
examples.trans: As one wise man said, the sun shines equally on everyone.

examples.text: Теперь весь ресторан полностью на мне.
examples.trans: Now the entire restaurant is completely on my shoulders.

examples.text: По поводу ресторана я тебе уже говорил, Дима.
examples.trans: I already told you about the restaurant, Dima.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'appointment' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да ничего, я опоздала на встречу из-за тебя.
examples.trans: It is nothing, I missed my meeting because of you.

examples.text: До встречи!
examples.trans: See you!

examples.text: У меня встреча.
examples.trans: I have a meeting.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да ничего, я опоздала на встречу из-за тебя.
examples.trans: It is nothing, I missed my meeting because of you.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!

examples.text: Мы опоздали из-за дождя.
examples.trans: We were late because of the rain.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Двадцать четыре часа в сутки работаю как раб.
examples.trans: I work twenty-four hours a day like a slave.

examples.text: Нет, Дима, тут ты совсем неправ.
examples.trans: No, Dima, you are completely wrong here.

examples.text: Состряпать может любой дурак, а ты попробуй приготовить!
examples.trans: Any fool can whip something up, but try to actually cook!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Итак, друзья, начинаем репетировать наш план!
examples.trans: Alright, friends, let's start rehearsing our plan!

examples.text: Кролик сырой, не рассчитаться ли нам по спору?
examples.trans: The rabbit is raw, shall we settle up on our bet?

examples.text: Итак, смотри внимательно.
examples.trans: So, look carefully.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Друзья, у Вики сегодня день рождения!
examples.trans: Friends, today is Vika's birthday!

examples.text: Мне друзей своих стыдно будет туда пригласить.
examples.trans: I will be ashamed to invite my friends there.

examples.text: Я сегодня утром с одним другом поспорил.
examples.trans: I made a bet with a friend this morning.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'begin', paired with 'начать'.

examples.text: Итак, друзья, начинаем репетировать наш план!
examples.trans: Alright, friends, let's start rehearsing our plan!

examples.text: Когда начинать?
examples.trans: When do I start?

examples.text: Урок начинается в девять.
examples.trans: The lesson starts at nine.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rehearse'.

examples.text: Итак, друзья, начинаем репетировать наш план!
examples.trans: Alright, friends, let's start rehearsing our plan!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и репетировать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to rehearse on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: О, наш повар наконец проснулся!
examples.trans: Oh, our cook has finally woken up!

examples.text: Это наша свадьба, где хотим, там и празднуем!
examples.trans: It is our wedding, we celebrate wherever we want!

examples.text: Если тебе стыдно, можешь на нашу свадьбу не приходить!
examples.trans: If you are ashamed, you do not have to come to our wedding at all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Думаешь, я не хотела дорогое платье и хороший ресторан?
examples.trans: Do you think I did not want an expensive dress and a good restaurant?

examples.text: Чтобы у тебя было дорогое и красивое платье.
examples.trans: So that you have an expensive and beautiful dress.

examples.text: Давайте снимем хотя бы ваш ресторан, я оплачу всё!
examples.trans: Let's rent at least your restaurant, I will pay for everything!

meanings.en: to go in, to come in, to enter
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go in, to enter', paired with 'войти'.

examples.text: Входит друг Димы, Лёва, пошёл!
examples.trans: In walks Dima's friend, Lyova, go!

examples.text: Входишь сразу налево.
examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left.

examples.text: Входите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Come in, please!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'went/am off', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: Дочка, ты пойми, свадьба — это один раз в жизни.
examples.trans: Sweetheart, understand, a wedding is once in a lifetime.

examples.text: Можно я пойду?
examples.trans: May I go?

examples.text: Пойдём домой.
examples.trans: Let's go home.
